note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a TRI 12; A06b TRI 12; L05 TRI 11(1), 11(2D), 17): ordinary naturalisation after 6 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: No provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states (the dataset codes no separate descent rule for a child born in the country, birth there giving it; the parent's sex is read from mode A01b). Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Trinidad and Tobago, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Trinidad and Tobago for 12 months immediately prior to the application, and was either resident in Trinidad and Tobago, or in government service, or had partly such residence and partly such service for 5 out of 7 years prior to the 12-month period. ... n.a. ... Person acquires citizenship of another country otherwise than by marriage. Does not apply to citizens by birth or by descent. Loss cannot result in statelessness. ... No provision ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born abroad to a citizen otherwise than by descent, or to a citizen in the service of Trinidad and Tobago.; Person is born abroad to a citizen by descent (registration by parent while person is a minor, or by the person him/herself within 1 year after reaching the age of majority). Person loses citizenship if oath of allegiance is not taken within 1 year after reaching the age of majority. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Trinidad and Tobago. Unless born to a foreign diplomat and neither parent is a citizen, or one of the parents is an enemy alien and the child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. ... No provision

Person loses citizenship if oath of allegiance is not taken within 1 year after reaching the age of majority.
